name: Leah Smith
life: “I still remember waiting on a late babysitter outside a closed salon.” Friday often includes a stop at the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, where Leah prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I thought a free manicure made it fair. The technician asked who would watch her sleeping children.
appearance: Leah has a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose. Look for close-cropped dark curls. Away from the heat of the kitchen, the familiar outfit is a gray fisher's sweater with a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand. In conversation Leah draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first.
personality: Leah admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Leah learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
agenda: To price childcare into the proposed evening.
family: Noel Berry is Leah’s cousin raised in the same household. Leah is free to hang up first. Noel makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The broken till*, Noel says, “I took a lunch for a patient and forgot to sign.”
connections: Sadie Carver. Paying for a babysitter is part of deciding which name can go on the staff letter.
